subtopics.title: Locate surds between integers
subtopics.exposition: If the n-th root of a number cannot be simplified to a rational number, it is called a surd. The square root of 2 and the cube root of 6 are surds, but the square root of 4 is not a surd because it can be simplified to the rational number 2. A perfect square is the number obtained when an integer is squared; for example 9 is a perfect square since 3 squared equals 9. A perfect cube is a number which is the cube of an integer; for example 27 is a perfect cube because 3 cubed equals 27. Consecutive integers are two integers that follow one another on the number line, for example 5 and 6 or 8 and 9. The position of a surd on the number line can be estimated without a calculator by saying which two integers it lies between; for example, the square root of 3 is above 1 and below 2 (a calculator gives 1.73205...). To place a cube root between two integers, find the perfect cubes on either side of the number under the root: the cube root of 52 lies between 3 and 4 because the cube root of 27 is 3, the cube root of 64 is 4, and 52 is between 27 and 64. To find the lower integer that the square root of 26 lies above, use perfect squares: 5 squared is 25, therefore 5 is less than the square root of 26. To find the upper integer that the square root of 26 lies below, use perfect squares: 6 squared is 36, therefore the square root of 26 is less than 6. Write the final answer as a single inequality joining the lower integer, the surd and the upper integer: 5 is less than the square root of 26, which is less than 6. To find the lower integer that the cube root of 49 lies above, use perfect cubes: 3 cubed is 27, therefore 3 is less than the cube root of 49. To find the upper integer that the cube root of 49 lies below, use perfect cubes: 4 cubed is 64, therefore the cube root of 49 is less than 4. Write the answer as a single inequality: 3 is less than the cube root of 49, which is less than 4. Check the answer by cubing all terms in the inequality and simplifying: 27 is less than 49, which is less than 64. This is true, so the cube root of 49 lies between 3 and 4. In this chapter the surds considered have the form n-th root of a, where a is any positive number, for example the square root of 7 or the cube root of 5. It is very common for n to be 2, so the 2 is usually not written: the surd is written as just the square root of a rather than the 2nd root of a.

subtopics.title: Rank numbers including surds
subtopics.exposition: If a and b are positive whole numbers and a is less than b, then the n-th root of a is less than the n-th root of b.
